2
Four students, A, B, C and D, have completed an experiment to determine the acceleration of
free fall, g. Each student repeated the experiment three times. The determined values of g are
shown in the table.
Which set of results has a high precision and a low accuracy?
acceleration of free fall / m s–2
experiment 1
experiment 2
experiment 3
A
7.2
9.4
8.3
B
9.5
9.8
10.2
C
9.8
9.8
9.9
D
10.1
10.2
10.1

hints: Look at the spread of the three $g$ values in $\text{m s}^{-2}$ for each student to judge precision - small range means high repeatability.
Recall that accuracy means closeness to the true value of about $9.81$ $\text{m s}^{-2}$, not closeness of the repeats to each other.
Compare the mean of each row with $9.81$ $\text{m s}^{-2}$ and check which row clusters tightly but clusters away from the true value.
walkthrough: Recall the definitions: precision is how closely repeated measurements agree with each other, while accuracy is how closely the mean agrees with the true value of $g \approx 9.81$ $\text{m s}^{-2}$.

Check the range for each student: A spans $9.4-7.2 = 2.2$ $\text{m s}^{-2}$, B spans $10.2-9.5 = 0.7$ $\text{m s}^{-2}$, while C and D each span only $0.1$ $\text{m s}^{-2}$, so C and D have high precision.
Estimate the mean for the two precise sets: C averages to about $9.83$ $\text{m s}^{-2}$ and D averages to about $10.13$ $\text{m s}^{-2}$.
Compare each mean to $9.81$ $\text{m s}^{-2}$: C is within about $0.1$ $\text{m s}^{-2}$ so it is accurate, whereas D is systematically about $0.3$ $\text{m s}^{-2}$ too high so it has low accuracy.
Therefore the set that is tightly clustered but displaced from the true value, showing small random error but significant systematic error, is student D. This is option D

A.explanation: Spread $7.2$ to $9.4$ $\text{m s}^{-2}$ is very large, so precision is low, and the mean near $8.3$ $\text{m s}^{-2}$ is far from $9.81$ $\text{m s}^{-2}$.

B.explanation: Values $9.5$, $9.8$, $10.2$ $\text{m s}^{-2}$ have only moderate precision and a mean near $9.8$ $\text{m s}^{-2}$, so accuracy is high.

C.explanation: Values $9.8$, $9.8$, $9.9$ $\text{m s}^{-2}$ agree very closely and average to about $9.8$ $\text{m s}^{-2}$, so both precision and accuracy are high.

D.explanation: Values $10.1$, $10.2$, $10.1$ $\text{m s}^{-2}$ agree within $0.1$ $\text{m s}^{-2}$ but average about $0.3$ $\text{m s}^{-2}$ above the true $g$, so precision is high and accuracy is low.
